What is the difference between a foundation trench and a trench?
A foundation trench is made for a strip footing, a trench for a whole project (e.g. a utility)
A trench is always deeper than 6 m
There is no difference, the two are synonyms
A foundation trench is always sloped, a trench is always shored
For a foundation: a foundation trench/pit; for a whole structure: a trench/excavation. A trench is narrow (typically 1–3 m), for linear works.
Which of these does NOT determine the size of an excavation?
The angle of internal friction of the soil

The size of the excavation is determined by the dimensions of the structure, the traffic and transport needs and the dewatering needs. The soil properties (e.g. the friction angle) affect the type of support.
Which is one of the four principles of equilibrium?
Tying back behind the soil mass to be retained
Internal support, embedment, own or mobilised weight, tieback – and combinations of these.

In cohesionless soil the slope inclination cannot be greater than the angle of internal friction. The exact value is given by a stability analysis.
Above what height should a berm be built into the slope?
For a higher slope, above 3–5 m, it is advisable to build a berm.
What surface surcharge can be taken into account (as a minimum) in the design of the slope according to the standard?
It is advisable to specify that nothing is stockpiled within the failure plane, but in design a surface surcharge of at least 10 kPa can be taken into account.
What is true of permanent excavation support?
It becomes part of the structure (e.g. underground car park, subway, tunnel)
It is always made of timber
It is removed once the structure is complete
The role of temporary support ends once the underground structure is complete; permanent support becomes part of the structure.
